title: Two device-side timers disagree by 31% on the same gfx1151 kernel, and the measurement that licensed this target's timing source was retained only as prose

evidence.retained: no campaign workspace: both measurements were taken by an authoring session against the device directly, not through a Campaign, so there is no run id or event sequence to cite. Re-running now to mint one would be a repair placed just before the check it satisfies. This record is the retention, and what it holds is stated in full below so a successor can compare rather than trust.
evidence.host: infplane, AMD Radeon Graphics (gfx1151, Strix Halo), ROCm 7.2.1, torch 2.9.1

hip_dispatch.device_reset: 256 MiB buffer zeroed before each timed dispatch

rocprofv3.device_reset: L2 flushed and synchronised before each roctx range opens

observation: The same kernel at the same shape reads 31.858us under the roctracer assay and 24.224us under a rocprofv3 kernel trace, a 31% gap, with both resetting the device and both reporting a device span. The most likely account is the per-dispatch instrumentation each tool adds, but nothing here measures that, so it is an account and not a finding. Neither number was retained anywhere when the timing source was declared: `tasks/devices.py` carried them as a comment and the rest lived in a commit message, which is the shape ADR 0065 names -- a declaration resting on the author session's own reported measurement. An independent reviewer could not re-run either and recorded them as unchecked.
proposed_change: Retain this record as the evidence the gfx1151 `timing_source` declaration rests on, and treat the gap as bounding what may be claimed: a ranking of two arms timed by one source under one policy is unaffected, because a fixed per-dispatch cost is common-mode and the sealed manifest declares one kernel per candidate. An absolute latency for gfx1151 is not supported by either number alone, and a latency taken under one source is not comparable with one taken under the other. Closing this properly means measuring the instrumentation cost rather than assuming it -- an empty-kernel cohort under both assays would do it.
